bull.b: Material deleveraging and positive equity provide a stronger capitalization base than in 2024. Lower debt can reduce fixed financial pressure and preserve more flexibility for research spending, although continued losses still weigh on overall financial resilience.

A focused pipeline of fibroblast-derived therapies gives the company a defined long-term development strategy in chronic diseases. Progress through preclinical and clinical programs could create future commercial opportunities if candidates demonstrate safety and efficacy.

The convertible debenture adds near-term cash to support ongoing operations and development activities. Its fixed conversion price and issuance limits can constrain immediate dilution, while scheduled repayment terms make the funding more structured than an unrestricted equity raise.

bear.b: The absence of revenue and persistently large losses show that the business remains pre-commercial and has not yet established an operating earnings base. Losses far above earlier periods indicate substantial investment needs and limited evidence of near-term self-funding.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means research and corporate activities consume cash rather than generate it. Combined with no revenue, this leaves operations dependent on additional financing and increases exposure to unfavorable funding terms over time.

The Nasdaq delisting process creates a structural trading and liquidity risk while the company works to regain compliance. Continued private financings and approved warrant-related share issuance also point to reliance on capital markets and potential dilution.
